requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
rationale:
I judged the reviewed tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. Each obligation maps to a test that asserts its outcome. I did not request implementation source, because the tests' assertions were enough to judge them.

- **Path form and empty selector.**
  - `selector.rs#mod[tests]/fn[parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments]` checks that `parse_selector("")` is empty. It also parses multi-segment paths and rejects malformed ones: `a//b`, `fn`, `[run]`, `fn[run`, `fn[run]x`.
  - `outline/tests.rs#fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]` asserts that `outline.resolve("")` is 0, the root.
- **Named segments `kind[name]`.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` assert many exact generated selectors. Each is resolved back to the node carrying that selector.
- **Anonymous segments `kind@hash`.**
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` asserts the selector equals `item@` plus `identity_hash[..12]`. It also asserts that identity_hash differs from structural_hash, and that the selector survives a descendant edit.
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts the `use@` plus 12-character form. It checks that selectors survive an insertion and that a changed `use` no longer resolves.
  - The parser test checks 12-hex-digit hashes and rejects `use@123`, `use@0123456789zz` and `use@0123456789abc`.
- **`#N` disambiguation.**
  - `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` asserts `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` map to source order. It also asserts that swapping the declarations swaps the ordinals.
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts duplicate `use` nodes get `#1` and `#2`.
  - The Rust tests assert that an unnumbered ambiguous selector, `fn[repeated]`, fails to resolve.
  - The parser test asserts `#0` is invalid and that `#2` and `#3` round-trip.
- **`line` exception.** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` asserts that identical lines have identical selectors, with no `#N`. It also asserts the selector resolves, and that whitespace-only differences share a selector while `two words` and `twowords` differ.
- **Percent-encoding.**
  - `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` asserts exact encoding of `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@`, space, tab, NBSP and U+3000 as UTF-8 bytes. It also asserts decode round-trips and rejects raw `/`, a raw space and a bad escape.
  - Generated selectors such as `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]` show the encoding in real outlines.
- **Multipart labels.**
  - The parser test splits `impl[Thing/Trait%3CT%3E]` into two parts.
  - It checks that `Segment::base` renders `impl[a%2Fb/c%20d]`.
  - `outline_content.rs#fn[selecting_multipart_impls_and_literal_slashes_preserves_label_boundaries]` checks that `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]` selects the impl. It also checks that `impl[Thing%2Fcore::fmt::Display]` and the markdown selector `section[A/B]` fail, while `section[A%2FB]` succeeds.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** The `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` test prepends blank lines. It asserts the selectors stay `fn[run]#1` and `fn[run]#2` while `line_start` changes.

I found no untested obligation and no marking gap. The structural-hash computation itself is cited context and was not reassessed.

text: :::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. In a multipart label such as `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `/` separates
name parts. A slash within one part is encoded as `%2F`. Line numbers MUST NOT
form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
